messages:
Nora (Mercury Health): Quick intro: Mercury's triage flow needs a claims NER + labeler for PHI/diagnoses. We
 like to run this in our VPC with HSM keys. Can Redwood help onboard?

Jamal (Customer Success): Hey Nora, yes we can. A few quick Qs: will you provide the model weights, and do you need real-time latency guarantees?

Nora (Mercury Health): We'll bring a tuned 13B artifact. Target p95 latency ~200ms or below for short docs.

Priya (Solutions Eng): Thanks. For sizing: approximate average token length, typical document size, and peak QPS?

Nora (Mercury Health): Docs vary 80-600 tokens; avg ~180. Steady QPS 5, peaks up to 30 during batch ingests.

Owen (Security): PHI note: Private VPC + HSM is required. We
 also want the E2E diagram and to confirm whether de-id happens before hitting the model.

Nora (Mercury Health): De-id happens upstream. We'll disable model-level logging/retention.

Kei (SRE): 13B with KV cache + warm workers should hit your p95 target. We'll recommend GPU family (A10x or similar). Also want to know acceptable cold-starts and recovery RTO. Multi-AZ preferred?

Nora (Mercury Health): Multi-AZ yes. RTO for critical paths < 2 mins. Cold starts should be rare.

Priya (Solutions Eng): For the first rollout, do you want no quantization to preserve entity recall? Rare entity recall is sensitive.

Nora (Mercury Health): Correct — recall for PHI > 99% on our eval sets. Hold off on quantization for v1.

Ava (Product): We'll run a staged rollout. Canary with synthetic traffic -> 10% -> 100%. We'll monitor entity recall delta and latency. Auto-rollback if recall drops > 0.5%.

Jamal (Customer Success): I'll capture this as action items. Nora: please upload a 500-sample redacted eval set and an eval spreadsheet (entity labels + expected outputs). Also send the dataflow diagram and KMS policy snippet.

redwood-intake-bot: Intake created: <https://console.redwood.ai/intakes/INT-2026-1199|INT-2026-1199> assigned to Jamal, Priya.

Priya (Solutions Eng): Sample eval runner (replace paths as needed):
```
# eval snippet
python -m redwood.eval --model /mnt/model --samples samples.json --metrics entity_recall,entity_precision,latency_p95 --batch 1
```

Owen (Security): Also: we need a signed NDA addendum for the PHI onboarding and confirmation that model artifacts will not be exfiltrated. Please add contact at your legal team.

Nora (Mercury Health): Legal contact is legal+redwood@mercuryhealth.com. We'll send the signed addendum and the KMS policy by EOD.

Kei (SRE): I'll propose autoscaling: 2 warm replicas, scale up by gpu_queue length, prefix cache TTL 30m for common reports. Priya: can you include token distribution histogram in sizing doc?

Priya (Solutions Eng): Will do. Also, what's your expected error handling policy? Can the app accept degraded responses (e.g., partial NER) during overload?

Nora (Mercury Health): No — downstream triage depends on full entity sets. If degraded, we prefer fail-closed (reject) rather than partial outputs.

Jamal (Customer Success): Scheduling a 30-min intake sync tomorrow 11am PT to walk through uploads and go/no-go checklist. Nora, that time work?

Nora (Mercury Health): Yep, confirmed. Thanks all! :raised_hands:

Ava (Product): Flagging this as renewal opportunity: if onboarding completes within 45 days and SLA met, likely contract expansion.

redwood-intake-bot: Reminder set for follow-up meeting: 2026-06-10T18:00:00Z.
